title: Errors in Recovering Drive from Disk Image
body: Hi all, A week back, I lost my keyfile for my laptop's encrypted SSD, and after thoroughly searching, decided to give up and just re-install Arch on it. Before I did, I made a disk image backup of the entire disk (both the unencrypted boot and encrypted root partitions), just in case I found the keyfile. Well I found the keyfile (it was in the one place I didn't check) and now I have the task of restoring the disk and putting it back in my laptop. I thought this would be easy, but when I restored the image to the disk, the partition table was corrupt, and it couldn't be read. I made the disk image with GNOME Disk Utility and restored it also using that, so maybe there was some issue with that? I can try restoring it using another method, but I'd prefer not to since it takes a long time. I tried a couple ways to restore the disk, starting with testdisk, which resulted in it finding this partition table, which looks correct (1GB EFI and 999GB LUKS partition) Disk /dev/nvme0n1 - 1000 GB / 931 GiB - CHS 953869 64 32 Current partition structure: Partition Start End Size in sectors 1 P EFI System 2048 2099199 2097152 2 P Linux filesys. data 2099200 1953525167 1951425968 When I saved it and restarted, the partitions showed up, however they were both labeled as 'unknown' by GNOME and Gparted, and couldn't be mounted. I tried to at least recover the EFI partition using fsck.fat, but this returned an error # fsck.fat -r /dev/nvme0n1p1 fsck.fat 4.2 (2021-01-31) Logical sector size (2028 bytes) is not a multiple of the physical sector size. I also tried to dump the LUKS header on the second partition, but that also returned an error # cryptsetup luksDump /dev/nvme0n1p2 Device /dev/nvme0n1p2 is not a valid LUKS device. Something else weird is that fdisk shows the disk identifier as all F's # fdisk -l Disk /dev/nvme0n1: 931.51 GiB, 1000204886016 bytes, 1953525168 sectors Disk model: WD_BLACK SN770M 1TB Units: sectors of 1 * 512 = 512 bytes Sector size (logical/physical): 512 bytes / 512 bytes I/O size (minimum/optimal): 512 bytes / 512 bytes Disklabel type: gpt Disk identifier: FFFFFFFF-FFFF-FFFF-FFFF-FFFFFFFFFFFF Device Start End Sectors Size Type /dev/nvme0n1p1 2048 2099199 2097152 1G EFI System /dev/nvme0n1p2 2099200 1953525167 1951425968 930.5G Linux filesystem I also tried mounting the image as a loop device, but it gave me the same errors and same problems, so it's not a physical drive issue. Please let me know what else I should try or if there is a known solution for this. I've looked around and I can't find anything about this specific issue. This is my first post so please let me know if there's other information I should have added or if I've done something wrong.
